target_customer: Consumers with mobile phones, plus carriers and advertisers
problem: People could not easily see where friends were or what was nearby from a phone.
business_model: Carrier distributed subscription and later free app with location advertising

founders.name: Sam Altman
education: Stanford University, sophomore when the prototype was built (per Wikipedia)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the founder.

founders.name: Nick Sivo
education: Stanford University, sophomore when the prototype was built (per Wikipedia)

competitors.name: Helio Buddy Beacon
competitors.what: Carrier service to locate friends using the GPS Drift phone
competitors.funding_then: Helio was a joint venture of SK Telecom and EarthLink

competitors.name: Dodgeball
competitors.what: Text message check in groups using zip code location

technical_complexity.rationale: Required carrier GPS integration and phone clients across many handsets, mostly integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Carrier distribution deals helped, but location sharing was copyable and depended on carriers and later on iPhone platform features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Location features arrived in larger platforms; Loopt sold to Green Dot in March 2012 and its products were to be shut down.

market_need_then: Carriers launched social mapping in 2006 (Boost Mobile with Loopt, Helio Buddy Beacon), and press covered the appeal and privacy debate; users reached 4 million by July 2010.

identity.voice_and_tone: Boost Mobile ads used the line Where you at

branding.brand_signature: Where you at? Boost Mobile ad campaign

rebrands.why: Wikipedia says the company was initially called Radiate; date and reason not stated.

brand_strength.rationale: Known mainly through carrier partners and press; no source shows iconic brand pull.

outcome_analysis: Loopt raised venture rounds from Sequoia and NEA, distributed through carriers such as Boost and Sprint, and reached 4 million users by 2010. Location sharing then moved into larger platforms and phones, and Loopt sold to Green Dot in March 2012 for 43.4 million dollars cash, of which 9.8 million was a retention pool, which looks like a team and technology acquisition more than a growth outcome.
notes: Series A date: Wikipedia is undated, an aggregator says 2005-11. Series B conflicts: Wikipedia 8.25M, an aggregator 12M. A 15M Series C in 2010-05 (post-money 60M) appears only on Dealroom, unverified, not recorded as a round. Wikipedia says more than 30M raised in total while CB Insights says 17M. Company site loopt.com returned HTTP 503 at fetch time. Trademark records show LOOPT marks owned by Loopt, Inc.
